about.title: {language}, **a little every day.**
about.intro: {app} is a free course for anyone who wants to speak {language}. {description} Short, game-like lessons take you from greetings to everyday conversations about family, food, the market, travel, health and more.
about.how: Each unit introduces a handful of words and phrases, then practises them in many ways: picking pictures, building sentences, listening, typing and matching. Words you find hard come back for review at the right time, and stories let you read along with the cast. Streaks, XP and a daily goal help you keep going.
about.account: There is nothing to sign up for. Your progress is saved on your own device, and the app keeps working offline once it has loaded. You can export your progress in [Settings](#/settings) to back it up or move it to another device.
about.ads: Lessons are free. To cover running costs, a few clearly marked sponsored cards may appear between sections of the path and after a lesson, never during one. See the [privacy policy](#/privacy) for how ads work.
about.open: The app is built in the open on [GitHub]({repo}). Corrections to the {language} are always welcome.

contact.title: Say **hello.**
contact.intro: Spotted a mistake in a lesson, have an idea, or a question about the app or its ads? We’d love to hear from you.
contact.email: Email us at [{email}](mailto:{email}). We usually reply within a few days.
contact.issues: You can also [open an issue on GitHub]({issues}). For a language correction, include the unit and the sentence so we can find it quickly.
contact.progress: We can’t see your progress, so if you’re asking about it, describe what happened in your message.

terms.title: Terms of **use.**
terms.intro: By using {app} you agree to these terms. If you don’t agree, please don’t use the app.
terms.use: {app} is free for personal learning. Please don’t try to disrupt the site, copy it to pass off as your own, or click ads on purpose to inflate them.
terms.data: Your progress lives in your browser. Clearing your browser data, or using a different device or browser, starts you afresh unless you export and import your progress. We can’t recover lost progress for you. See the [privacy policy](#/privacy) for more.
terms.ads: The app may show ads from Google AdSense, always marked Sponsored. Products and services in ads come from their advertisers, not from us, and we don’t endorse them.
terms.content: We work hard to keep translations accurate, but languages vary between speakers and regions and mistakes happen. The course is offered as it is, without any warranty. The app’s code is published on [GitHub]({repo}).
terms.changes: We may update the app and these terms. When the terms change, the date at the top changes too. Questions? [Contact us](#/contact).

privacy.title: Your data **stays with you.**
privacy.keep: {app} has no accounts and no server of its own. Your name, avatar, progress, streak, XP and settings are saved in your browser’s local storage on this device. We never see them. You can export, import or erase them at any time in [Settings](#/settings).
privacy.adsOn: {app} is free and is supported by ads from Google AdSense.
privacy.adsOff: {app} may show ads from Google AdSense to stay free.
privacy.adsWhere: Ads appear only in a few places, such as between sections of the learning path and on the lesson complete screen, and are always marked **Sponsored**. They never appear inside a lesson, practice session or story.
privacy.cookies: Google and its partners use cookies to serve ads. If you choose _Allow_, Google may use cookies to show ads based on your visits to this and other websites. If you choose _Basic ads only_, Google shows non-personalised ads, though it may still use cookies to limit how often an ad appears and to prevent fraud. You can change your choice in [Settings](#/settings) at any time.
privacy.google: Learn more in [how Google uses information from sites that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites), and manage personalised ads at [Google Ads Settings](https://adssettings.google.com).
privacy.offline: When you’re offline, no ads are loaded.
privacy.pixelOn: We use the Meta Pixel to see whether our Facebook and Instagram ads bring new learners.
privacy.pixelOff: We may use the Meta Pixel to see whether our Facebook and Instagram ads bring new learners.
privacy.pixel: It loads only if you choose _Allow_ on the Facebook card or in [Settings](#/settings). When allowed, Meta receives which screens you open, when you finish onboarding, when you finish a lesson (its type and XP) and streak milestones, along with what your browser normally sends, such as your IP address and Meta cookies. Your name, avatar, answers and progress are never sent. Choose _No thanks_, or switch it off in Settings, and nothing more goes to Meta.
privacy.fonts: Text is set in fonts served by Google Fonts, so your browser requests them from Google the first time you visit. After that they’re cached on your device.
privacy.weather: If you turn on _Weather on the crane_ in [Settings](#/settings), your browser asks for your location once. It is rounded to about 10 km, kept on this device, and sent to [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com) at most once an hour to get the local weather. Open-Meteo needs no account and sets no cookies. It’s off unless you turn it on.
privacy.children: We don’t knowingly collect personal information from anyone. Because ads may be personalised only with your consent, parents can choose _Basic ads only_ for younger learners.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it. Questions? [Contact us](#/contact).
